introduction.problem_before: A wallet payment or a mempool broadcast calls RpcClient::send. If the node answers late or not at all, one lost reply fails the whole call with Timeout and the wallet UI shows “offline”.
introduction.change: send tries up to 3 times with exponential backoff (200 ms, doubling, capped at 4 s, plus jitter), then gives up with the new Exhausted error.
introduction.example_before_after: Before: send() → Err(Timeout) after one attempt. After: send() → attempt 1 times out → wait about 200 ms → attempt 2 → Ok.

steps.title: Trigger: callers of send
steps.called_by: a user action in the wallet or the relay (outside the diff)
steps.decides: Nothing here; it builds the request and calls client.send.
steps.why: Shows who reaches the retry loop, in particular a call that is not safe to repeat.

annotations.text: broadcast_tx now reaches a retrying send.
Not visible in this repository: does the node reject a repeated broadcast_tx for the same transaction, so that a second send is harmless?

assessment.reason: This context step submits one request; repetition is introduced by the downstream retry decision.

steps.title: Attempt: build the request and send once
steps.decides: Counts the attempt; rebuilds the request on every turn.
steps.why: The counter feeds the retry decision; the request is rebuilt because execute consumes it.

annotations.was: Built the request and sent it once.
annotations.is: Builds and sends once per loop turn; the turn count is kept in attempt.

annotations.text: Every attempt gets the full per-attempt timeout, so the worst case is 3 × timeout plus delays.

assessment.reason: The attempt counter and request construction are local; the retry decision controls whether another request is sent.

steps.title: Outcome of the attempt?
steps.decides: Branches on the result: Ok, Timeout, other error.
steps.why: Only timeouts are retried; every other error keeps the old behaviour.

annotations.was: execute(...).await? returned every error to the caller.
annotations.is: match on the result with three outcomes.

assessment.reason: Only timeouts take the new path; success and other errors return directly.

steps.title: Return the response
steps.why: A successful attempt ends the loop at once.

annotations.is: Returns the response from any attempt.

assessment.reason: This unchanged return exits the loop immediately without another send.

steps.title: Retry allowed?
steps.decides: Asks RetryPolicy::should_retry(attempt); yes goes to step 6, no goes to step 7.
steps.why: The loop needs a rule for when to stop; the rule is a plain attempt limit.

annotations.was: No retry decision; the timeout went straight to the caller.
annotations.is: Retries while attempt < max_attempts (3). The method of the request is not an input.

annotations.text: mempool::broadcast_tx may submit the same transaction twice if attempt 1 reached the node and only the reply was late.
should_retry receives only the attempt number and no method or idempotency input: can broadcast_tx be sent twice when the reply arrives late?

assessment.headline: A wallet user could see one payment broadcast twice after a slow node reply; an operator would see duplicate-transaction rejections in the node log.
assessment.reason: A repeated value-moving request at system scale (wallet and relay both call send). It needs a reply delayed past 5 s, which flow 2 makes more likely.
assessment.basis_note: read 4 files (client.rs, retry.rs, mempool/mod.rs, wallet/pay.rs); nothing executed
assessment.smallest_correction: Pass an idempotency input into should_retry (or skip retry for broadcast_tx); add a test with a transport that delivers the request and then times out.

steps.title: Wait, then try again
steps.why: Spaces the attempts so a briefly overloaded node can recover.

annotations.is: Sleeps backoff(attempt): 200 ms doubling, capped at 4 s, plus jitter; then loops to step 2.

annotations.text: With jitter applied after the cap, can one sleep exceed max_delay (4 s)?

assessment.reason: Latent: the 4 s cap is out of reach while every client uses the default of 3 attempts, and no setter can change it.

steps.title: Give up: Exhausted
steps.decides: Returns the new error instead of Timeout.
steps.why: Callers need to tell a retried failure from a single timeout.

annotations.is: Returns Err(Exhausted { attempts }) once the policy refuses another attempt.

annotations.text: Callers that matched on Timeout no longer see it from send; wallet::fetch_balance maps only Timeout to WalletError::Offline.
Two wildcard sites were found (flow 3): do all callers of send still handle the case that used to be Timeout?

assessment.headline: Wallet users get a generic RPC error instead of the “offline” message once retries run out.
assessment.reason: User-visible message change on a common failure; no data is affected.
assessment.smallest_correction: Map Exhausted to the same wallet error as Timeout.

steps.title: Other errors returned as before
steps.why: Only timeouts are worth another attempt.

annotations.is: Returns any non-timeout error at once.

assessment.reason: The existing error return remains separate from the timeout retry path.

steps.title: Client holds a retry policy
steps.called_by: every caller that builds an RpcClient
steps.decides: Stores RetryPolicy::default() in the new retry field.
steps.why: send needs a policy; new gives every client the default of 3 attempts.

annotations.is: Every client carries a RetryPolicy, set to the default in new.

annotations.text: No setter or constructor argument takes a policy: how does a caller that must not retry change it?

assessment.reason: Policy construction is bounded to client setup; retry exposure is assessed at the decision step.

steps.title: Retry policy: attempt limit and delays
steps.decides: Allows attempts while attempt < max_attempts; computes the delay before the next attempt.
steps.why: The loop needs a rule for when to stop and how long to wait; both live in one policy value.

annotations.was: No retry rule; util::backoff had only the MAX_ATTEMPTS constant.
annotations.is: should_retry allows another attempt while attempt < max_attempts (3).

annotations.text: Jitter is applied after the cap, so one delay can exceed max_delay by up to half; with the default 3 attempts the delays are 200 ms and 400 ms before jitter and never reach the cap.

assessment.reason: The default attempt limit bounds the loop; the send and jitter steps carry the concrete concerns.

thread_statuses.reason: should_retry still retries every method, broadcast_tx included.
The line now calls with_jitter; the random draw it refers to lives in jitter_fraction, moved in flow 5.
